info.name: TradePulse Pay
info.description:
TradePulse Pay HTTP endpoints and the PayPal **sandbox** calls the app makes.

1. Import this collection and `TradePulse-Pay-sandbox.postman_environment.json`.
2. Set `clientId` / `clientSecret` (your own sandbox app) locally. No secrets are stored in these files.
3. Run "OAuth 2.0 access token" first; it fills `accessToken`.

Orders and Payments go through `@paypal/paypal-server-sdk` in the app; Payouts, Invoicing and webhook verification use plain REST (see `docs/apimatic-log.md`). All writes carry a `PayPal-Request-Id`.

request.description: Liveness probe for the Convex HTTP router (`convex/http.ts`). Returns 200 with JSON `{status: "ok", app, timestamp, version}`. Public, no auth.
Plain-text discoverability manifest for AI agents (`convex/http.ts`). Lists the app's public endpoints. Public, no auth, cached for one hour.

item.name: PayPal webhook: unsigned replay of a sample event

request.description:
Replays a sample `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED` event **without** PayPal signature headers (`paypal-transmission-id`, `paypal-transmission-sig`, `paypal-cert-url`, `paypal-auth-algo`, `paypal-transmission-time`).

**Documented result:** HTTP 400 with `{"error": "Missing PayPal signature headers."}`. Nothing is processed. The delivery is recorded in the `paypalEvents` table as `verified=false`, `processed=false` with the reason (`convex/payments/webhook.ts`, `recordUnverifiedEvent` in `convex/payments/webhookDb.ts`).

Every real delivery is checked with `POST /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature` before any state changes, so a forged or simulated event can never move money. PayPal dashboard simulator events also fail verification by design and get the same 400.

Other responses: 413 for bodies over 256 KB, 400 `Body is not a PayPal webhook event.` for a body without `id`/`event_type`, and 503 when `PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID` is unset or PayPal's verify endpoint is unreachable (so PayPal retries a genuine event).

Check the row: `npx convex run payments/webhookDb:recentEvents '{"limit":5}'`.

exec: pm.test('unsigned replay is rejected with 400', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));

item.name: PayPal webhook: replay the same event id again (dedupe)

request.description:
Sends the same unsigned event again with the same `id` (`{{replayEventId}}`).

**Documented result:** HTTP 400 again, and the table still holds exactly one `paypalEvents` row for that event id: `recordUnverifiedEvent` never inserts a second row or overwrites an existing one.

**Dedupe for signed events:** when PayPal redelivers a verified event whose row is already `verified=true, processed=true`, the endpoint answers 200 `{"ok": true, "duplicate": true, "changed": false}` and does not reprocess it (`processVerifiedEvent` in `convex/payments/webhookDb.ts`). A row left by an earlier unverified or failed delivery is upgraded in place, so there is still one row per event id. A verified delivery cannot be produced from Postman because it needs PayPal's signature.

exec: pm.test('unsigned replay is rejected with 400', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));

request.description:
LLM proxy used by the AG Studio payments dashboard chat (`convex/dashboard/studioProxy.ts`). The browser sends one AG Studio LLM request per turn; the proxy calls Anthropic with the key held in the Convex environment and streams NDJSON AG-UI events back. The AI only explains and proposes; it never moves money.

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer {{convexAuthToken}}` with a Convex Auth JWT of a signed-in GC or Owner. Copy it from the browser after signing in (local storage key starting with `__convexAuthJWT`). With `convexAuthToken` empty the documented result is 401 `{"error": "Not authenticated: sign in required."}`; a sub's token gets 403; 503 if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is not configured.

item.name: PayPal sandbox
item.description: The sandbox REST calls the app makes, in workflow order: token, fund (create + authorize), release (capture), close (void), pay the sub (payout), change-order invoice, webhook verification.

request.description: Client-credentials token for the sandbox REST app (`PayPalClient` token cache in `convex/payments/paypalClient.ts`; the Server SDK reuses the same token through `oAuthTokenProvider`). Basic auth with `{{clientId}}` / `{{clientSecret}}` from your own sandbox app; values are never committed. The test script stores the token in the `accessToken` collection variable for the other PayPal requests. Run this first.

header.description: Idempotency key. The app derives it from the payment row (see description).

request.description: Orders v2 create with `intent: AUTHORIZE`, as `createFundingOrder` does through `OrdersController.createOrder` (`convex/payments/orders.ts`). The app sets `reference_id` = milestone id, `custom_id` = payment id and `PayPal-Request-Id` = `fund_<milestoneId>_<attemptNo>`. Funds are only held, not captured. Approve the order in a browser with the logged approve link (guest card 4032031427005060, 01/29, CVV 480) before calling Authorize.

exec: if (approve) console.log('Approve as guest buyer at: ' + approve.href);

header.description: Idempotency key. The app derives it from the payment row (see description).

request.description: Places the hold after buyer approval, as `authorizeFundingOrder` does through `OrdersController.authorizeOrder` (`convex/payments/orders.ts`, request id `<idempotencyKey>_auth`). Returns `purchase_units[0].payments.authorizations[0]` with `id`, `status` and `expiration_time`; the app stores the honor period as `create_time` + 3 days. Without buyer approval PayPal answers 422 `ORDER_NOT_APPROVED`. The test saves `authorizationId`.

exec: pm.test('authorized, or not yet approved by the buyer', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 201, 422]));

header.description: Idempotency key. The app derives it from the payment row (see description).

request.description: Release & pay: captures part of the hold, as `captureApproved` does through `PaymentsController.captureAuthorizedPayment` (`convex/payments/captures.ts`, request id `cap_<key>`). `final_capture` is true only when the amount equals the remaining authorized amount. Only `COMPLETED` or `PENDING` captures count as paid.

header.description: Idempotency key. The app derives it from the payment row (see description).

request.description: Releases the uncaptured remainder of the hold, as `voidRemainder` does through `PaymentsController.voidPayment` (`convex/payments/captures.ts`, "Close milestone"). Returns 200 with the voided authorization, or 204 with `Prefer: return=minimal`. A fully captured authorization cannot be voided (422).

exec: pm.test('voided, or nothing left to void', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 204, 422]));

header.description: Idempotency key. The app derives it from the payment row (see description).

request.description: Payouts v1 create, plain REST (the Server SDK has no Payouts controller), as `payoutSub` does in `convex/payments/payouts.ts`. The app uses the payment idempotency key as both `PayPal-Request-Id` and `sender_batch_id`, and sends the net amount after retainage. A repeated `sender_batch_id` returns 400 `USER_BUSINESS_ERROR` with a link to the existing batch, which the app treats as an idempotent hit. 422 `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` is retried on a bounded schedule. The test saves `payoutBatchId`.

Payouts v1 batch status, as `refreshPayout` and the `pollPayoutBatch` scheduler do (`convex/payments/payouts.ts`). The item `transaction_status` (`SUCCESS`, `UNCLAIMED`, `FAILED`, ...) decides the payout state, because an unregistered receiver is `UNCLAIMED` while the batch says `SUCCESS`.

header.description: Idempotency key. The app derives it from the payment row (see description).

request.description: Invoicing v2 create, plain REST, as `invoiceChangeOrder` does (`convex/payments/invoices.ts`, body from `buildInvoiceBody` in `convex/payments/changeOrderMath.ts`). Request id `co_<changeOrderId>_create`. The sandbox returns 201 with a `href` whose last path segment is the invoice id; the test saves `invoiceId`.

header.description: Idempotency key. The app derives it from the payment row (see description).

request.description: Sends the draft invoice to the Owner (`convex/payments/invoices.ts`, request id `co_<changeOrderId>_send`). The sandbox sends no email; the app stores the payer-view URL instead. Returns 200 with a `href`, or 202.

Invoice detail and status (`getInvoice` in `convex/payments/invoices.ts`, used by "Refresh status"). `detail.metadata.recipient_view_url` is the payer-view link shown to the Owner; `status` becomes `PAID` after payment.

The check `/paypal/webhook` runs on every delivery (`verifyWithPayPal` in `convex/payments/webhook.ts`). Fill the `webhook*` variables with the `paypal-*` headers of a real delivery and your sandbox webhook id. Returns 200 `{verification_status: "SUCCESS" | "FAILURE"}`; with the placeholder values it returns `FAILURE` or 400, which is the same outcome the unsigned replay gets.
